investigations.name: influenza-crossparadigm
investigations.title: Influenza cross-paradigm — one Sego 2022 blueprint, three mechanical substrates
investigations.description:
This investigation is the capstone of the `viva-multicell-blueprint` build: it
ties together the backend-neutral blueprint (Task 17), the `compile(blueprint,
backend)` compiler (Task 13), both real backends running the full model (fields
Task 6, rules Task 7, systemic ODE fed live by CellCountStep Task 21, immune
recruitment via latent-pool activation Task 20, real footprints Task 19), the
comparison layer (`viva_multicell_blueprint.compare` — identity, raster, metrics)
and the three interactive figures (`viva_multicell_blueprint.viz`).

**Blueprint update.** The recruitment design (Task 20) activates a PRE-PLACED
LATENT immune pool, so the Sego blueprint's `initial_state` now pre-places 12
size-25 latent immune cells (M/NK/CD8_latent) at the tissue margins via
`extra_blocks`; the `infected_seed` is scoped to the main epithelial block so the
latent pool never changes the infected count. All cells are size 25 (size-9 cells
dissolve). Parameters stay faithful to Sego 2022 params.yaml @ b952eec2.

**Runnable artifact.** `viva_multicell_blueprint.composites.sego.sego_crossparadigm`
(a `@composite_generator`, parameterized by `backend` and `blueprint`) is the
baseline composite for every study and drives the dashboard Composite Explorer.

**Reduced scale.** Every study runs at a TRACTABLE reduced scale (a 50x50-site
patch, a 6x6 epithelial block) so the runs actually complete; this is a
demonstration, not paper scale. The comparison is reproducible (fixed seeds).

**Third paradigm (center-based).** A third mechanical substrate — a center-based
model (viva-munk / pymunk: each cell a circular rigid body, area-matched to the
blueprint `size`) — is now compiled from the SAME canonical blueprint via
`local:MunkBackend`, visualized as a third panel in every spatial playback, and
scored PAIRWISE (cpm↔vertex, cpm↔munk, vertex↔munk) in the equivalence and
counterfactual studies. It is deliberately NOT calibrated to the other two
(docs/mechanics.md §3), so it is a genuinely independent representation.

**Anti-goal respected.** No parameter is tuned to force the backends to agree.
Honest divergence is reported.
investigations.question: Can ONE backend-neutral blueprint express the whole Sego 2022 influenza model (ViralInfectionVTM) and run it faithfully on three different mechanical substrates — a Cellular Potts model (viva-cpm), a vertex model (vivarium-tyssue), and a center-based model (viva-munk) — and where do the substrates agree vs diverge when the shared mechanism is driven live?
investigations.hypothesis: Because the field / rules / systemic-ODE / latent-pool recruitment mechanism is compiled BYTE-FOR-BYTE identically onto all three backends and only the single mechanics node differs, cell-FATE dynamics should be nearly backend-independent, while SPATIAL morphology should diverge — each substrate samples the shared field at its own cell centroid and measures cell-cell contact through its own geometry. Divergence is therefore expected and is a finding about the substrate, not a bug. (Confirmed three-way: fate agreement is statistically EQUIVALENT across all three paradigm pairs, while spatial agreement is not — and the center-based model, which is not calibrated to the other two, is the most spatially divergent of the three.)

investigations.name: composite-gallery
investigations.title: Viva-munk Composite Gallery
investigations.description: A gallery of the nine viva-munk multi-cell composites, each run as its own study with a simulation animation and a short biological write-up.
investigations.question:
Can every viva-munk composite from the published report be reproduced as an individual,
runnable study in the dashboard, with its simulation GIF shown on the report?
investigations.hypothesis:
Each composite, run with the demo defaults, qualitatively reproduces its published panel —
surface attachment, pressure-limited bending growth, biofilm packing, chemotactic gradient
climbing, mother/daughter device kinetics, nutrient-coupled growth, inclusion-body aging,
and density-dependent quorum sensing.
